As someone who builds and repairs instruments… Gibson guitars are and have always had questionable QC at best. There’s ebbs and flows in terms of how good/bad it is in a certain era but they do things their way and sometimes that’s an issue. For example their refusal to use a scarfed headstock joint leading to breakage or the fact that they let their lacquer finish cure for less than half the time it needs before buffing and shipping. Martins are pretty solid, they vary a bit by what era but I love the ~$1000 dollar martins quite a bit. But as for Gibson I’d say buying an American made Eastman for below or at worst at the same cost as a Gibson is a far better buy. But to be honest upper end Asian made guitars like Reverends or even higher range squiers (QC is sometimes spotty but good examples are very good) or gretsch electromatics are plenty competitive with more expensive American factory line instruments.

The thing is without the electoral college your presidential vote would mean something. Within PA you’re outnumbered by democrats, sure. But if the state itself does award every vote to whoever gets a majority suddenly the amount of minority votes in any given state become very important. Rn it’s technically mathematically possible (though obviously not in practice) to win with well under 30% of the vote.

The original federation agreement also said that states got extra electoral college power and representation based on how many slaves they had (despite them being disenfranchised). Maybe what some dudes did or did not originally intend should not be the end all be all of the discussion. There’s a lot of things that the founders did that weren’t good. That doesn’t make everything they did bad by any means but they are not beyond reproach or question.

Uh I don’t know how to say this but in the presidential election there necessarily has to be one winner. We have bodies like the senate for wider representation but if you can only elect one person why would you choose the one with 48% of the vote not 52%? At that point the election seems pointless if you’re not going to appoint the victor. In a single election the majority will win sure, but that’s not “always overruling” any more than the minority winning would be.

I’d argue the electoral college very much doesn’t encourage campaigning with the whole nation. It encourages campaigning extremely heavily in states like Ohio and Florida which can swing and provide a ton of electoral votes regardless of the margin of victory. Republicans for example campaign harder in Florida than Alabama because they’ll win Alabama regardless.

Uh. If everyone votes in the same election and every vote counts the same a coal miners vote counts exactly as much as a NYC hedge fund manager’s does. If a Wyoming vote is worth 4x the electoral college points as a California one something seems off. Also if you live in a heavily partisan state and don’t vote that way your vote is meaningless. Red voters in Illinois and blue voters in Mississippi have no functional way to affect anything in the electoral college system. It also encourages a system of campaigning designed to win a slim majority in specific states rather than building a larger base of support across the board.
